page: Microsoft Azure FX24-6mds_v2 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. It features 6 vCPUs across 3 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache. The server is equipped with 504.0 GB of RAM, yielding an exceptionally high memory density of 84.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a 1417 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core and text processing capabilities. The server achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2362.0 and a text processing score of 2948.0, both placing in the top 10% tier. Single-threaded gzip compression at 34.83 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.37 GB/sec also perform in the top 25%. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics generally fall into the average range, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 6660.14 and uncached large-block read bandwidth of 51.2 GB/sec.

A notable performance tradeoff is observed in large-scale machine learning tasks. LLM text generation for a medium 7B model is poor at 4.59 tokens/sec, and prompt processing for a 70B model is weak at 5.65 tokens/sec, reflecting the lack of dedicated GPU hardware. Given the massive memory-to-vCPU ratio and strong single-thread performance, this server is suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, in-memory caching, and text processing tasks that do not require heavy parallel GPU acceleration.
